Welcome This vault is a practical Obsidian handbook and a starter knowledge system. Use it as: a syntax reference a study workflow guide a mathematics and programming note handbook a template library an example vault Start with Getting Started , then keep Quick Reference nearby. Core idea Write useful notes first. Organize them enough to find them later. Link concepts when a connection is genuinely useful. ercise → exam review  The vault becomes a study system rather than a collection of disconnected notes.

Markdown MOC Standard Markdown/CommonMark-style syntax is the foundation. Some items below are Obsidian extensions, especially ==highlight== . Headings Formatting Highlights Lists and Tasks Quotes and Rules Tables Links Images Code Blocks Footnotes Comments HTML Escaping Characters Related Wikilinks Embeds ect access to the main Markdown features.

Code Blocks Use fenced code blocks with a language identifier. ```python def square(x): return x * x ``` Common identifiers: python java javascript cpp c html css sql bash json yaml mermaid Related: Programming MOC , Mermaid Basics , Code Block CSS it Change the language tag from python to text and look at the highlighting.  Highlighting disappears; the language tag controls it.

Comments Obsidian supports two comment syntaxes. Both stay in the Markdown source but are hidden in Reading view. %% Obsidian comment: hidden in Reading view. %% <!-- HTML comment: also hidden in Reading view. --> Multi-line Obsidian comment: %% This whole block is hidden. It can span several lines. %% Portability note %% … %% is Obsidian-only. <!-- … --> also works in other Markdown tools, so prefer it for notes you may export. A code comment ( in Python, // in Java) is different: it is part of the code, not Markdown. Related: HTML , Properties ows only: An array starts at index 0. The reminder stays in the file, so you can find it with the search TODO .

Escaping Characters Use a backslash to prevent Markdown punctuation from being interpreted. \ *not italic\* \ not a heading \[not a link\] Common characters that may need escaping: \ * _ ` [ ] ( ) > + - . ! Escape only when needed; unnecessary escaping reduces readability. ic*  Write \ not a heading at the start of a line, then remove the backslash.  With the backslash it stays plain text; without it, it becomes a heading.

Footnotes A statement with a footnote.[^1] [ ^1 ]: Supporting detail. Inline footnotes can also be written as: A statement.^[Short supporting note.] Use footnotes for references or side details that would interrupt the main flow. t. 1  Add a second footnote [^2] and click each marker.  Each marker jumps to its own definition at the bottom. It is commonly used for structured plain-text documents. ↩

Backlinks Obsidian: Backlinks show notes that link to the current note. They help answer: Where is this concept used? Which lessons depend on this idea? Which notes should I revisit? Use backlinks for discovery, not as a replacement for deliberate navigation. Related: Wikilinks , Knowledge Graph g Variables shows Python in its Backlinks panel.  Open Conditions and look at the Backlinks pane.  Every note that links to it is listed, without editing Conditions.

Block Links Obsidian: A block reference points to a specific paragraph, list item, or other block. Give a block an explicit ID by placing ^id at its end: This paragraph can be referenced. ^important-point Link to it: [[Note#^important-point]] Embed it: ![[Note#^important-point]] Obsidian can also generate block IDs through its UI when available. Related: Embeds , Wikilinks  link opens the exact block containing The stack follows LIFO .  Add ^lifo-rule to a sentence and link it from another note.  The link opens that exact paragraph.

Bookmarks Obsidian: a core plugin that pins notes, searches, headings or graphs for quick return. Use bookmarks for the few pages you open every day (your course MOC, the Quick Reference), not for everything. Add one from a note's ⋮ menu → Bookmark… , then open the Bookmarks panel in the sidebar. Related: Quick Switcher , Workspaces mark reruns the search.

Callouts Obsidian: Callouts are a native Obsidian Markdown extension. Built-in types > [!NOTE] > Text > [!TIP] > Text > [!IMPORTANT] > Text > [!WARNING] > Text > [!DANGER] > Text > [!CAUTION] > Text > [!INFO] > Text > [!ABSTRACT] > Text > [!TODO] > Text > [!SUCCESS] > Text > [!QUESTION] > Text > [!FAILURE] > Text > [!BUG] > Text > [!EXAMPLE] > Text > [!QUOTE] > Text Renders as: Note note Text Tip tip Text Important important Text Warning warning Text Danger danger Text Caution caution Text Info info Text Abstract abstract Text Todo todo Text Success success Text Question question Text Failure failure Text Bug bug Text Example example Text Quote quote Text The type controls the callout style/icon. Types are case-insensitive. Some names are aliases of a main type (for example IMPORTANT shares the tip style and CAUTION shares the warning style), so two callouts can look the same. Custom title > [!TIP] Exam shortcut > Memorize this identity. Renders as: Exam shortcut tip Memorize this identity. Foldable Add + to start expanded or - to start collapsed: > [!NOTE]- Details > This starts collapsed. > [!TIP]+ Details > This starts expanded. Renders as: Details note This starts collapsed. Details tip This starts expanded. Nested content Indent content under the callout: > [!NOTE] > Main point. > > - Item A > - Item B Renders as: Note note Main point. Item A Item B Nested callouts > [!QUESTION] Why? > The outer explanation. > > > [!TIP] > > A useful hint. Renders as: Why? question The outer explanation. Tip tip A useful hint. Practical combinations > [!IMPORTANT] Definition > A compact definition. > [!WARNING] Common mistake > Do not confuse [[Conditions|if]] with [[Boucles|while]]. > [!EXAMPLE] ked example example Substitute the known values first. Keep callouts purposeful: definitions, warnings, decisions, Reference, and key takeaways. Related: Highlights , Properties , Mathematics Example  == .  Fold the callout by changing [!warning] to [!warning]- .  It starts collapsed and expands on click.

Good uses: concept maps project architecture lecture synthesis brainstorming visual planning For persistent knowledge, keep important information in normal Markdown notes and use Canvas as a visual layer. Command Palette Obsidian: The Command Palette exposes commands from core features and installed plugins. Open it from the command palette hotkey, commonly Ctrl/Cmd + P . Use it to discover commands instead of memorizing every menu location. Related: Hotkeys , Workspaces d is created.  Search "daily" in the palette.  You see the Daily Notes commands (if the core plugin is on).

Daily Notes Obsidian: Daily Notes creates/opens a note for the current date. A practical daily note can contain: 2026-09-09 # Focus - [ ] Main task # Notes - # Review - What did I learn? - What remains unclear? Use Daily Note Template as a simple starting template. File Recovery Obsidian: a core plugin that keeps automatic snapshots of your notes so you can restore an earlier version. By default it takes a snapshot every few minutes and keeps them for a limited number of days (both configurable in its settings). It is a safety net for mistakes, not a backup: see Backup and Sync . Open it from the Command Palette: File recovery: Open version history . Related: Command Palette , Backup and Sync estore the first one.

Graph View Obsidian: a core plugin that draws notes as nodes and links as lines. See Knowledge Graph for how to use it well. Useful settings: Filters: show only a folder ( path:"10 - " ) or a tag. Groups: colour notes by folder or tag. Local graph: shows only the neighbours of the open note. Related: Backlinks , Knowledge Graph , and the links of those notes.

Outline Obsidian: a core plugin that lists the headings of the open note in the sidebar. Click a heading to jump to it. Good headings ( Headings ) make the outline a table of contents for free. Related: Aliases and Heading Links , Workspaces ew scrolls to that heading without manual scrolling.

Properties Obsidian: Properties are structured metadata stored in YAML at the top of a note. Example: --- title: Boucles course:  I type: concept status: active tags: - programmation -  aliases: - Boucle --- Common property types include text, lists, numbers, checkboxes, dates, and links. Practical properties --- type: lesson course:  I status: todo date: 2026-09-09 tags: - university --- Tips Use a small stable vocabulary. Use properties for data you may search, filter, or query. Do not turn every sentence into metadata. Community plugins such as Dataview can query properties. son course =  status = active  Add status: done and change it to todo .  The property panel and search [status:todo] follow the change.

Quick Switcher Obsidian: a core plugin that opens a note by typing part of its name. Default hotkey: Ctrl + O ( Cmd + O on macOS). Type a few letters, press Enter to open. Shift + Enter creates the note if it does not exist. Aliases from Properties are searched too. Related: Command Palette , Hotkeys , Search ens by its alias as well as its title.

Search Obsidian: Search is a core feature with operators for narrowing results. Useful Reference: "exact phrase" tag:#programming path:"04 - Programming" file:Python line:(TODO) [status:active] task-todo task-done Combine terms: tag:#university path:"03 - Mathematics" Tips Search before creating a duplicate note. Use exact phrases for definitions. Use path: when a folder matters. Use properties/tags consistently if you expect to filter by them. Related: Tags , Organization MOC , Search Strategy ch uses square brackets: [property:value] .  Search [status:active] in your vault.  Only notes with that exact property value are listed.

Tags Obsidian: Tags classify notes and are searchable. #programming #programming/python #university/ Tags can also be stored in Properties: --- tags: - programming - programming/python --- Practical rule Use tags for broad, reusable classification. Use Properties for structured fields such as status , course , and date . Related: Search , MOCs the tag pane.  Search opens with every note carrying that tag.

Tasks Native Obsidian supports Markdown checkboxes: - [ ] Review loops - [x] Finish exercise 4 You can search for tasks using search queries such as: task-todo task-done For advanced task queries, recurrence, and task-focused workflows, see the community plugin Tasks Plugin . Related: Search , Daily Notes e to complete.  Search task-todo after adding two tasks.  Both unchecked tasks appear in the results.

Templates Obsidian: The core Templates plugin inserts predefined Markdown into notes. Typical workflow: Create a Templates folder. Enable the core Templates plugin. Set its template folder. Insert a template into a new note. See Templates MOC . For programmable templates, see the community plugin Templater . r i in range(3): print(i)  Every new lesson starts with the same structure instead of being rebuilt manually.  Insert the template into an empty note.  The note gets the empty structure only, no example text.

Web Clipper Official extension: Obsidian Web Clipper is a browser extension (not a core plugin). It saves a web page as a Markdown note in your vault. Use it to keep a documentation page or an article you want to summarise. Clip, then rewrite the key points in your own words (see Atomic Notes ). Check the extension's own page for supported browsers and current features. Related: Images , Attachments  find where the note came from.

Wikilinks Obsidian: Wikilinks are Obsidian's internal-link syntax. [[Note]] [[Note|Display text]] [[Folder/Note]] For a heading: [[Note#Heading]] [[Note#Heading|Display text]] For a block: [[Note#^block-id]] Tips Type [[ and search for a note. Rename notes through Obsidian to keep internal links updated. Prefer meaningful links over linking every noun. Related: Aliases and Heading Links , Block Links , Backlinks ote name.  Obsidian suggests matching notes; pick one to insert the link.

Workspaces Obsidian: Workspaces save layouts of panes, tabs, and views. Useful layouts: Study: notes + outline + backlinks Coding: concept + code + terminal/editor outside Obsidian Review: note + backlinks + search Save layouts when switching contexts frequently. Related: Command Palette , Daily Notes ult The three panels reopen in the same arrangement.  Save a second layout called Coding with one pane.  You can switch between both layouts from the palette.

Callout CSS Theme/CSS-dependent: this changes callout appearance without changing callout syntax. Example scoped to a custom callout type: .callout [data-callout= "study" ] { border-left-width : 4px ; } Use it with: > [!study] Study > Review this before the exam. Custom callout types depend on Obsidian's callout handling and your CSS. Test them after theme changes. Related: Callouts , CSS Snippets snippets. Write the callout: > [!study] Exam tip > Review this before the exam.  The callout is rendered with your custom study style instead of the default note style.

Code Block CSS Theme/CSS-dependent: code block styling varies by theme. A conservative example: .markdown-rendered pre { overflow-x : auto; } Avoid changing syntax highlighting colors unless you are prepared to maintain theme compatibility. Related: Code Blocks , CSS Snippets hon remains exactly the same logically: Hello  Enable a snippet that adds padding, then disable it.  The code and output text never change.

CSS Snippets Theme/CSS-dependent: CSS snippets modify presentation; they do not change Markdown semantics. Keep snippets small and scoped. Example: /* Slightly constrain readable line width */ .markdown-preview-view , .markdown-source-view { --file-line-width : 900px ; } Exact selectors can change across Obsidian/theme versions. Disable a snippet if it causes unexpected layout changes. Related: Themes , Callout CSS l result Text using .study-important appears bold.  Toggle the snippet off in Settings → Appearance.  The style disappears; the note is unchanged.

Hotkeys Obsidian: Hotkeys are configurable per vault. Use Settings → Hotkeys to assign shortcuts to frequently used commands. Good candidates: command palette quick switcher templates daily note search Avoid assigning dozens of shortcuts. Memorize only high-frequency actions. Related: Command Palette , Workspaces ng Ctrl + O opens the quick switcher, so you can jump to any note by typing part of its name. ( Ctrl/Cmd + P already opens the Command Palette by default.)  Assign a key to "Toggle left sidebar".  The key now toggles the sidebar.

Table CSS Theme/CSS-dependent: table appearance is controlled by the theme and CSS. A small readability tweak: .markdown-rendered table { width : 100% ; } Do not force complex responsive behavior unless you have tested it on both desktop and mobile. Related: Tables , CSS Snippets it Add width: 100% and compare.  The table stretches to the page width.

Themes Theme-dependent: themes change appearance and may introduce their own CSS/classes. Choose a theme from Obsidian's Appearance settings. Before relying on theme-specific styling, test the vault in the default theme. Keep content portable by avoiding theme-dependent formatting when possible.
